text:
Here he passed on foot through these streets,

without employment or post and without a peso.

Only poets, whores, and drunks

knew his verses.


He was never abroad.

He was in prison.

Now he is dead.

He has no monument...


But

remember him when you have concrete bridges,

great turbines, tractors, silver granaries,

good governments.


Because in his poems he purified the language of his people,

in which one day trade agreements will be written,

the Constitution, love letters,

and decrees.

translation.title: Here He Passed on Foot Through These Streets
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the poet's poverty and imprisonment against the future public language he helped purify.
